source:
Create a clean, low-poly 3D room inspired by an mechanical keyboard escape room game. 

Environment Setup:
- Room: A cozy, modern room with dark wooden walls, soft ambient LED strip lighting along the ceiling edges, and a large wooden desk in the center.
- Desk Setup: On top of the desk, place a massive 3D mechanical keyboard made of individual blocky keycaps (30% scale larger than the player character).
- Keycaps: Each keycap (letters A-Z, Spacebar, Enter, Backspace) must be an individual, separate Model named "Key_[Letter]" (e.g., "Key_A", "Key_Space"). The keycaps should have white caps with black labeled text on top, smooth plastic material, and sit slightly raised inside a keyboard frame.
- Door & Lock: Opposite the desk, place a sealed metallic door with a 6-digit glowing digital display keypad next to it.
- Decoration: Add a desk lamp with warm light, a small potted succulent plant, and a pair of headphones on a stand to set a calm ASMR vibe.

Mechanics & Layout Requirements:
- Space keys properly in a standard QWERTY layout.
- Ensure key models are structured so their top part can be moved downwards along the Y-axis when pressed.
- Leave an open walking area between the desk and the escape door.

image_prompt.text: Individual pressable keycaps across the giant mechanical keyboard, plus a 6-digit glowing digital keypad mounted beside the door
A feature surface in the player natural camera path carrying the hint toward the 6-digit code
A sealed metallic door that stays shut until the code is solved
A barrier that opens only once an earlier step in the puzzle chain is complete

a massive 3D mechanical keyboard of individual blocky keycaps on a large wooden desk in the centre of the room, 30 percent larger than the player character, spaced in a standard QWERTY layout, white caps with black labels on smooth plastic, raised slightly inside a keyboard frame
dark wooden walls with soft ambient LED strip lighting running along the ceiling edges
a desk lamp with warm light, a small potted succulent, and a pair of headphones on a stand

layout_placement.text: Every keycap and the 6-digit keypad register as pressable puzzle inputs
Carryable key items the solve inputs are waiting for
an open walking area kept clear between the desk and the escape door

notes: The whole game is indoors, so Sealed Chambers routes P0 rather than P3.

Each keycap must be a separate Model named Key_A, Key_Space and so on, with its top able to travel down the Y axis when pressed. This is a per-object naming and rigging requirement the layout handoff has no field for.
Preset caveat: Escape Room brings carryable key items and a second sequenced gate, and this fully enumerated single room has no place for either. Both are kept but flagged.

open_questions.ask: What links the keycaps to the door - do you type a word on the giant keyboard to reveal the 6-digit code, or is the code hidden somewhere in the room?

theme: Cozy Modern Low-Poly - dark wood, warm ambient LED strips, calm ASMR mood

answers.answer: Type a word on the giant keyboard to reveal the 6-digit code on the door display; the prompt does not call for hidden-room clues.
